newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bond yields reluctantly nudge higher.
newsitem.headline: Australian bond yields reluctantly nudge higher.

text.p: *Australian bond yields edged higher at the opening, largely reflecting weaker U.S. and neighbouring New Zealand debt markets
*Reluctance to sell locally pre-CPI on Wednesday
Australian bond yields edged higher at the start of trading, largely as a reflection of weaker U.S. and neighbouring New Zealand debt markets.
"There is some nervousness as the kiwi market gets hammered again, but we are still reasonably bullish and have priced in a good CPI for tomorrow," one bond trader said.
A renewed attack by U.S. sellers on the New Zealand dollar saw N.Z. yields spike up as the market once again attempted to keep monetary conditions within the RBNZ's desired level.
U.S. Treasuries also remained jittery ahead of Fed chairman Alan Greenspan's semi-annual Humphrey-Hawkins testimony.
Greenspan will deliver the first leg of his mandatory testimony to the House of Representative at 1800 GMT (4.00 a.m. Sydney time Wednesday).
However, there is a reluctance to sell Australian debt ahead of the second quarter local inflation report on Wednesday, which could fuel calls for a monetary policy easing.
Median forecasts centre on a 0.1 percent quarterly fall for the headline CPI and a 0.4 percent rise for the underlying rate.
"We should make 93.500 (on 10-year bond futures) on this sort of outcome, but to go any further inflation would have to be at the low end of expectations," one trader said.
The lowest forecast for inflation in a recent Reuters survey of economists was minus 0.3 for the headline rate and plus 0.2 percent for the underlying rate.
The market will also have to negotiate the second quarter average weekly ordinary time earnings report on Thursday before calls for a cut in current official 5.5 percent interest rates intensify.
In the meantime, HSBC Markets will be releasing its latest report on wages at 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT), while the Westpac leading index is due at 2.30 p.m. (0430 GMT).

Local yield spreads to N.Z. narrowed sharply, but they were modestly wider to North American markets, reversing some of Monday's trend. A local inflation outcome at or below median expectations could see initial support at 25 basis points on the 10-year yield differential tested, analysts said.
